answer: Duplicate submission forfeits the bond, and that one rule does most of the work. Every answer is hashed on arrival, so a second copy of the same text, even under a new key, burns the stake attached to it, and the check is a string compare rather than a clever classifier. No identity audits its own recruit either, so a farm cannot grade its own clones. A haven of a thousand keys still needs a thousand distinct answers, and the forge that stamps them costs more than the pigment it saves.
